cards.title: Top of the Ladder
cards.instruction: Carry yourself as the highest-status person present. Treat questions as requests for your approval.

cards.title: A Kinder Version
cards.instruction: Protect someone from the full truth by offering a carefully edited explanation that feels kinder than complete honesty.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll decide how we handle this. Nina's keeping her birthday dinner small. You and I can get noodles.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Small? She invited the whole choir.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You can question the details after my decision. She's choosing people she sees every week. It isn't a verdict on your friendship.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: We rehearse together every Tuesday. Read me her message.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: She wants an uncomplicated evening. That's the kindest accurate sentence. Come have one with me.

relationship.evidence: B2 and B4 know facts that test A's kindness and ask for actual text.

heightening.evidence: A5 stops inventing selection criteria and offers the least hurtful sentence plus company.

brevityWit.evidence: A5 kindest accurate sentence is explicit editing; the A3 generic hierarchy phrase is clumsy.
